title: “IF YOU LOVE ME, KEEP MY COMMANDS”—BUT WHAT IF WE HAVE BEEN HEARING JESUS WRONG?
paragraphs:
“IF YOU LOVE ME, KEEP MY COMMANDS”—BUT WHAT IF WE HAVE BEEN HEARING JESUS WRONG?
The frightening difference between obeying Jesus to make Him love you…and obeying because His love has already captured your heart.
There is a sentence Jesus spoke that has comforted some Christians…and quietly terrified others.
“If you love me, keep my commandments.” — John 14:15, KJV
Maybe you have heard that verse preached like a warning.
If you really love Jesus, prove it.

And somewhere along the way, a sentence spoken by Jesus in one of the most tender conversations of His earthly ministry can begin sounding like the voice of an angry supervisor standing over frightened employees.
But something happens when you slow down long enough to hear Jesus in His actual context.
Because Jesus was not standing before a crowd of arrogant Pharisees when He spoke these words.
He was sitting with men whose world was about to collapse.
Judas had already gone into the darkness.
Peter was about to deny Him.
Jesus had told them He was leaving.
And into that atmosphere Jesus said:
Then He spoke about the Father.
About not abandoning them as orphans.
That changes the temperature of John 14:15 completely.
“Ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτέ με, τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσετε.”
“Ean agapate me, tas entolas tas emas teresete.”
“If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.”
The word translated “love” comes from ἀγαπάω — agapaō.
The word for “commandments” is ἐντολάς — entolas.
And the word translated “keep” in the widely accepted critical Greek text is τηρήσετε — tēresete — from τηρέω, meaning to keep, guard, observe, preserve, or hold fast.

There is an ancient textual variation here worth acknowledging rather than hiding. Some Greek witnesses read τηρήσατε, giving the force “keep my commandments,” while major critical editions read τηρήσετε, “you will keep my commandments.”
Either way, the surrounding teaching of Jesus makes the relationship unmistakable.
Love for Christ and obedience to Christ cannot finally be separated.
But here is where wounded people often misunderstand Him.
Jesus is not teaching that obedience purchases His love.
He is teaching that genuine love for Him expresses itself in obedience.
Those are not the same thing.
“Obey so Jesus might finally love you.”
“You have encountered a Savior so worthy of love that following Him begins changing what you want to do.”
“Perform, and perhaps you will be accepted.”
“In Christ, you have been loved at a cost you could never pay. Now follow the One who loved you enough to die for you.”
And maybe somebody reading this needs that distinction more desperately than they realize.
But you also know what you did last night.
You remember the words you said.
The addiction nobody at church knows about.
The resentment you keep feeding while smiling through worship songs.
The relationship you know is pulling you away from God.
The hidden habit you have promised God seventeen times you would never return to…and somehow you returned again.
So when Jesus says, “If you love Me, keep My commandments,” something inside you collapses.
Jesus continues by speaking of the Father giving His disciples “another Comforter” who would remain with them—the Spirit of truth.
“I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” — John 14:18, KJV
The Greek word translated “comfortless” there is ὀρφανούς — orphanous.
Jesus is essentially telling these frightened disciples:
I am not abandoning you like fatherless children.
John 14 is not Jesus throwing terrified sinners an impossible command and walking away.
He connects love with obedience…and then promises divine help.
He promises they will not be abandoned.
That does not make obedience optional.
Jesus never lowered holiness to make sinners comfortable.
The same Christ who forgives adultery says to leave the life of sin.
The same Christ who welcomes sinners calls people to repentance.
The same Christ who receives the broken also commands us to deny ourselves, take up our cross, and follow Him.
Grace is not permission to remain unchanged.
Grace is the power of God meeting people who could never rescue themselves.
And this is where modern Christianity sometimes wants half a Jesus.
A cross that removes guilt without a cross that puts the old self to death.
We want Jesus to forgive what we refuse to surrender.
But biblical love does not say:
“Jesus understands, therefore nothing needs to change.”
“Jesus understands…and because He loves me, He refuses to leave me enslaved.”
Read Jesus a few verses later.
“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me…” — John 14:21, KJV.
“If a man love me, he will keep my words…” — John 14:23, KJV.
“He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings…” — John 14:24, KJV.
What you do when nobody sees you matters.
What you refuse to surrender matters.
Not because flawless behavior earns the Father's affection.
But because a heart captured by Christ cannot peacefully make rebellion its permanent home.
There is a difference between struggling with sin…and making peace with it.
A struggling Christian can relapse into an old pattern and crawl back to God ashamed.
A struggling Christian may sometimes wonder how someone who loves Jesus could still be capable of such ugliness.
Jesus did not meet Peter after the resurrection and say:
“Peter, apparently you never cared about Me.”
And what question pierced Peter's heart?
And a broken disciple discovering that his worst chapter was not the final chapter Jesus would write.
Jesus restored Peter…and then called Peter to follow Him.
That is the difference between condemnation and conviction.
“You are unable to cleanse yourself, so come to the One whose blood cleanses sinners.”
Condemnation wants you hiding behind another religious mask.
The fact that you have been posting Bible verses while privately drifting away from the God whose Word you post.
Repentance is not paying Jesus back.
Repentance is turning from sin toward the Savior who alone can rescue you from it.
And that means John 14:15 should disturb something in us.
There is a counterfeit Christianity that wants assurance without transformation.
Jesus gives us no permission for that.
First John says that knowing God is connected with keeping His commandments.
“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” — 1 John 5:3, KJV.
Obedience is not the price tag attached to God's love.
It is fruit growing from a life being transformed by that love.
You do not tape apples onto dead branches and declare the tree alive.
Fruit comes because there is life inside.
In the same way, Christian obedience is not spiritual costume jewelry hanging from a corpse.
Things you once enjoyed without conviction started troubling you.
Things you once justified became harder to defend.
You started wanting holiness even while discovering how incapable you were of producing it by sheer willpower.
And sometimes transformation looks less glamorous than Christian social media makes it appear.
Sometimes obedience is deleting a number while crying.
Sometimes it is confessing what you hoped would remain hidden forever.
Sometimes it is forgiving somebody who never apologized.
Sometimes it is turning off the screen.
Sometimes it is ending the relationship.
Sometimes it is refusing to send the message.
Sometimes it is getting out of bed and praying when God feels painfully silent.
Sometimes obedience is whispering through tears:
“Jesus, I don't want to surrender this…but I want to want You more.”
That prayer may not sound impressive.
Because Jesus is not looking for religious actors who have mastered the vocabulary of Christianity while protecting private kingdoms He is forbidden to touch.
Because love without obedience eventually becomes sentiment.
We would recognize this anywhere else.
Imagine someone repeatedly telling his wife:
But he rejects everything covenant love requires.
And Jesus deserves infinitely more than sentimental Christianity.
He is not an accessory to our preferred lifestyle.
But here comes the part that keeps this truth from crushing repentant sinners.
The Gospel is not the story of good people proving how much they love Jesus.
It is the story of sinners discovering how unimaginably Jesus loved them first.
Before your obedience ever became evidence of love…
His cross became the demonstration of His.
You did not bear the nails.
You did not carry the judgment your sin deserved.
You did not conquer the grave.
That is why the cross destroys both pride and despair.
Pride cannot survive because you could not save yourself.
Despair does not get the final word because Jesus came to save people exactly as helpless as you.
At Calvary, sin is exposed as more terrible than we wanted to believe…and grace is revealed as more astonishing than we dared to imagine.
Your sin was serious enough that Christ had to die.
His love was great enough that He willingly did.
And somewhere between those two realities, your excuses begin dying.
“How much sin can I get away with and still go to heaven?”
“How can I keep giving myself to something that nailed the One I love to a cross?”
That is a radically different Christianity.
You are no longer negotiating the minimum requirements of discipleship.
You are falling in love with Jesus.
And love begins rearranging the house.
Sometimes the old nature will scream.
Sometimes you will discover wounds underneath sins you thought were merely habits.
Sometimes sanctification will feel painfully slow.
But the question is no longer whether you have achieved flawless performance.
When Jesus puts His finger on something, do you ultimately want Him more than you want the thing He is asking you to surrender?
Maybe you have spent years saying:
But perhaps while reading this, something already came to mind.
What if the most important thing you do after reading this article is not sharing it?
What if the most important thing is closing your eyes and finally telling Jesus the truth?
“Lord, I have called You Savior while resisting You as Lord. Forgive me. I cannot change myself. I need Your mercy. I need Your Spirit. Teach me to love You enough to obey You.”
That prayer matters infinitely more than any engagement this article receives.
Because Gospel Warrior cannot save you.
A Christian book cannot save you.
A church membership cannot save you.
And when you fall, do not turn your failure into an excuse to abandon the Savior.
There is no glory in pretending you never fell.
There is enormous grace in discovering that Jesus can restore a repentant sinner who thought the story was finished.
Not by pretending the scandal never happened.

Jesus rewrites everything by taking guilty, broken, rebellious people and doing what they could never do for themselves—redeeming them, forgiving them, restoring them, and transforming them into people who increasingly desire the One they once resisted.
If this exposed something you have been hiding, you do not need to describe your sin publicly.
Somebody underneath this article may need to discover they are not the only Christian fighting a battle behind a smiling profile picture.
And then think of one person.
The person whose name appeared in your mind while reading this.
Maybe they think Christianity is nothing but rules.
Maybe they believe grace means obedience no longer matters.
Maybe shame has convinced them Jesus is finished with them.
Maybe they still say they love Christ while protecting the very thing that is destroying their fellowship with Him.
Because there will probably be another night when obedience hurts.
Another moment when you need to remember:
You are not obeying Jesus to purchase His love.
You obey because Christ loved you first…and His love is teaching your heart that He is better than what sin promises.
Stay close to daily Scripture, biblical truth, conviction, encouragement, healing, discipleship, and spiritual nourishment centered on Jesus Christ.
And if you believe work like this should continue reaching people with the Gospel, you can help carry it.
Not because financially supporting a ministry proves that you love Jesus.
Scripture does not give us permission to make that claim.
And certainly not because God can somehow be purchased.
Support should flow freely from gratitude, stewardship, generosity, and a sincere desire to help biblical resources reach more people.
More opportunities to put biblical truth in front of the exhausted believer at 2:00 in the morning.
The woman wondering whether God can still use her.
The unbeliever who somehow stopped scrolling when the name Jesus appeared.
Because perhaps somebody in your world needs to discover what you just discovered:
“If you love Me, keep My commandments” is not Jesus demanding that terrified sinners perform well enough to purchase His affection.
It is the voice of the Savior who is worthy of everything.
The Savior who sends the Spirit.
The Savior who refuses to leave His people as orphans.
The Savior who forgives repentant sinners.
The Savior who transforms those who belong to Him.
And maybe tonight you finally need to stop asking:
“Do I obey enough for Jesus to love me?”
“Since Jesus has loved me like this…what am I still refusing to give Him?”
Because the command you have been afraid of may actually be exposing the idol you have been protecting.
And the Savior asking for your surrender is the same Savior whose scarred hands prove He withheld nothing when He came to rescue you.
You may have failed to keep your grip on Jesus—but the nail-scarred hands of Jesus are still calling you out of hiding and back into obedience.
